title: Synthetic demo: unwinding shells, two vintages per trace
attribution: Synthetic data generated by seismic_art (no real survey)
notes: amplitudes are relative; compare within this file only

phase is the unwrapped instantaneous phase of the analytic signal: one turn per cycle of the wavelet; instantaneous frequency is its rate and is meaningless where the envelope is below 20% of the trace's maximum

the monitor is read at the base's traces, moved by +4.02 ms and scaled by 0.98, both measured over 140-270 where nothing in the earth should have changed (median lag of 6 trace pairs; a constant offset between two processings is not a change in the earth)
the grain: after those corrections the two vintages still differ by an NRMS of 0.27 (correlation 0.97) in that window; a difference deeper down must be read against it
6 traces on a 2 x 3 grid, 60-1100 ms; inside the changed patch: IL 166/XL 374

synthetic truth: the monitor differs from the base inside one round patch of 450 m radius (thin-bed reflections weakened by 40%, every boundary below the top 3 ms earlier), has new noise everywhere, and was written one sample (4 ms) late

the second spiral is the monitor's instantaneous phase on the same radius; the opening between the spirals is the monitor's phase minus the base's, positive where the monitor lags (its event is later); a lag of 2 to 3 ms at 30 Hz is 20 to 30 degrees of turn
